summary: Regression backend test after removal of emergentintegrations and jq from backend/requirements.txt. Backend started cleanly with no ImportError. Full pytest suite (45 tests) passes 100%. DNC endpoint now correctly accepts empty {} body, missing body, and body with only 'reason' (all return 200). XLSX exports (openpyxl) produce valid zip-magic files. Telegram/email mock integrations work without external services.

minor.issue: When called with body {'reason': '...'} the response object does not echo back the 'reason' field (returns None). The value is likely stored on the DNC log but not on the org document; minor UX / API-contract inconsistency — clients cannot verify reason was captured without a separate GET.

Lockout identifier is `ip:email`; K8s ingress uses ≥2 pod IPs so each source IP builds its own counter. Not a security hole but delays lockout (still detected after ~20 attempts). Consider per-email or X-Forwarded-For normalization (unchanged from iteration_1).

action_items: OPTIONAL (minor): include 'reason' in the JSON response of POST /organizations/{id}/dnc, or document that reason is stored only in the dnc log.

Deployment on Render should now be unblocked — verified backend imports and boots without emergentintegrations/jq. Recommend a smoke test on Render post-deploy hitting /api/auth/login, /api/dashboard, /api/export/all.
critical_code_review_comments: backend/requirements.txt cleanup verified: no remaining references to emergentintegrations or jq in any backend/*.py or routers/*.py. grep is clean.
server.py imports cleanly under python 3.11 with the trimmed requirements.txt (verified via direct import).

backend/worker.py process_queue still lacks atomic findAndModify — carry-over from iteration_1; two concurrent processors (bg loop + manual /queue/process) can still race under real (non-mock) send. Fine for MOCKED demo.
routers/organizations.py — build_query uses raw user input in $regex without re.escape() (carry-over). Minor injection/DoS risk with metacharacters.
routers/imports.py — no file-size or row-cap on /import/upload (carry-over). A malicious multi-MB XLSX can OOM the backend on Render's small instance.
